How to Process a Leave Request

Responsible Teams and Roles
HR Operations, Payroll, People Managers

Leave Request Processing Runbook

Purpose
This runbook explains how HR should intake, evaluate, approve, and document employee leave requests, including medical leave, parental leave, bereavement leave, and unpaid personal leave.

When to Use
Use this runbook when an employee requests planned or emergency leave or when a manager notifies HR of a potential protected absence.

Responsible Roles
Primary owner: HR Operations specialist.
Supporting roles: Payroll, People Manager, HR Business Partner.
Approver: HR Business Partner or HR Manager for exceptions or complex compliance cases.

Procedure
Step 1: Record the leave request date, employee information, location, leave type if known, and expected duration.
Step 2: Review eligibility based on tenure, location, schedule, and applicable law or policy.
Step 3: Request required supporting documents or certification and communicate deadlines clearly to the employee.
Step 4: Notify the manager of the intake while preserving confidentiality and limiting sensitive information.
Step 5: Determine whether the leave appears to be protected, company-sponsored, paid, unpaid, or mixed.
Step 6: Coordinate with Payroll on pay treatment, benefit deductions, and any schedule coding changes.
Step 7: Issue written approval, provisional approval, or denial with explanation and next steps.
Step 8: Document return-to-work expectations, check-in timing, and any accommodation review needed before return.
Step 9: Update the HRIS case record with all decisions, dates, and communications.
Step 10: Before closure, confirm the employee has either returned, extended the leave appropriately, or separated under approved process.

Approval Requirements
Routine leave approvals may be handled by HR Operations within policy.
Complex cases involving legal ambiguity, accommodations, or multi-jurisdictional rules require HR Business Partner review.
Managers may not independently deny potentially protected leave requests.

Completion Criteria
The leave case is complete when the leave determination is documented, payroll handling is aligned, and the return or extension path is clearly recorded.
